Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

## Plan Changelog

**2026-08-22**: Plan created (7 child work items, test-first ordering, Medium effort/Medium risk).

## Plan Summary

This work item decomposes the upgrade economy fix into 7 child tasks with test-first ordering:

### Phase 1: Unit Tests (test-first, no dependencies)
- **CG-0MT407BKP000J4N9** — Unit tests: upgrade action economy

### Phase 2: Core Engine Wiring (parallel with browser tests)
- **CG-0MT40APW6003MSCT** — Engine: wire action cost into upgrade commands

### Phase 3: Implementation (3 parallel tracks)
- **CG-0MT40EHB1005JP6D** — Engine: implement hand-first click flow + target selection
- **CG-0MT40FT21005GBK7** — Engine: implement drag-drop buy-and-play
- **CG-0MT40HTYN008TJ6Q** — AI and Monte Carlo: budget-aware upgrade actions

### Browser Tests (test-first, parallel with implementation)
- **CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC** — Browser tests: hand-first click flow for upgrades
- **CG-0MT40GTSU006C6U1** — Browser tests: drag-drop and premium for upgrades

### Phase 4: Integration & Polish
- **CG-0MT42HHAB000VJUK** — Update existing tests, E2E, and documentation

### Dependency Graph
```
CG-0MT407BKP000J4N9 (unit tests)
       |
       v
CG-0MT40APW6003MSCT (engine: action cost)
    /      |       \
   v       v        v
CG-0MT40EHB1005JP6D  CG-0MT40FT21005GBK7  CG-0MT40HTYN008TJ6Q
(hand-first flow)    (drag-drop)           (AI/MC)
       \                |                /
        \               |               /
         v              v              v
        CG-0MT42HHAB000VJUK (update tests/E2E/docs)

CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC (browser: hand flow) ---\
CG-0MT40GTSU006C6U1 (browser: drag-drop) ----/
       |
       +-- blocks respective implementation children
```

## Problem statement

Playing an upgrade card currently costs **no action** and never passes through the hand — a market upgrade click applies the upgrade directly to the first eligible business (`buyUpgradeCommand` → `purchaseUpgrade`, no `consumeAction()`). This diverges from the business-card economy (move-to-hand = 1 action, same-day place free, held-card play = 1 action, drag-drop buy-and-place = 1 action + 50% premium) and gives upgrade cards a free second daily action. Upgrades should behave like business cards: go to the hand first when bought by click, with drag-and-drop as the same-turn buy-and-play path.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want playing an upgrade card to consume one of my daily actions like every other purchase/play **so that** the action economy stays honest (1 action/day, 2 with General Manager) and upgrades aren't a free lunch.
- **As a player**, I want upgrades I buy to land in my hand first **so that** I can choose when and where to apply them (target a specific business, possibly next day).
- **As a player**, I want to drag an upgrade straight from the market onto a business when I'm sure **so that** I can buy-and-play in one turn at a +50% premium, exactly like business buy-and-place.
- **As a player**, I want to pick which business to upgrade when playing from hand **so that** I can respond to my current street layout (e.g. branches / multi-level chains).

## Acceptance Criteria (Parent)

- [ ] **Action cost — click path:** Clicking a market upgrade moves it to hand and consumes 1 action; playing the same-day moved upgrade applies it with no additional action; playing a held-from-previous-day upgrade consumes 1 action. All paths decrement actionsRemaining and legality gates reject the action when the budget is spent.
- [ ] **Hand-first + target selection:** Upgrade market cards follow the two-step hand flow — never applied directly from the market on click. When an upgrade is selected in hand, the player clicks an eligible business on the street to apply it; ineligible targets are rejected with illegal-move feedback.
- [ ] **Drag-drop same-turn:** Upgrades in the market are draggable onto eligible street businesses — drag-drop = buy & play in the same turn, consumes 1 action, and charges the +50% premium. Illegal drops snap back with feedback.
- [ ] **Free ops unchanged:** Event cards' free move-to-hand and free play stay free; refresh, sell, hint, discard, community favour, end-turn remain non-action operations.
- [ ] **AI + Monte Carlo:** MainStreetAiStrategy and MainStreetMonteCarlo account for the upgrade action cost in budget-aware valuation, and remain deterministic per seed.
- [ ] **Testing/validation:** New unit tests cover action spend + gating for all three upgrade paths; browser tests cover the hand-first click flow, drag-drop onto eligible/illegal targets, and action-budget dimming; existing upgrade tests updated to the new flow.
- [ ] **Docs:** All related documentation updated; full project test suite (npm test) and npm run build pass.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing action economy: 1 action/day (2 with General Manager) — upgrades must not create a second implicitly-free action.
- Same-day composite stays free (consistency with business cards); the 50% premium formula must match the business buy-and-place exactly.
- Undo/redo must wrap the new paths (snapshotted commands; new actions after undo invalidate the redo stack).
- State/transcript/save-load fields must stay consistent (e.g. justMovedHandCardId semantics generalise to upgrades; pendingUpgradeIndex-style state added if needed).
- Reduced-motion and mute settings must be respected by any new animation/SFX.

## Effort and Risk

- **Effort:** Medium (37.83h recommended, range [26h-57h])
- **Risk:** Medium (score 10/25, confidence 74%)

# Intake Brief: Main Street — Banking-Aware AI Strategy (Deliberate Action Hoarding)

## Problem Statement

Main Street's AI strategies (GreedyStrategy, RandomStrategy) consume the daily action budget greedily every turn with no concept of action banking. Since action banking (CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR) lets unused actions persist across days (capped at 2), the AI never conserves actions — it spends everything and loses the remainder. Banking is therefore a human-only strategic tool. The AI needs a deliberate hoarding strategy that banks actions on some days to enable bigger multi-action plays later (e.g., move-to-hand + buy-and-place combo, premium placement), with look-ahead depth and aggressiveness that scales down at lower difficulties.

## Users

- **Players** of Main Street — they expect the AI opponent to use the same strategic tools humans have, making games feel strategically deep and fair at each difficulty.
- **TCE developers / producers** — need the banking-aware AI to be testable (unit + Monte Carlo), balanceable by difficulty, and cleanly separated from the existing Greedy strategy.

Example user stories:

- "As a player on Medium/Hard, I want the AI to occasionally skip a low-value spend to bank an action for a high-value play I can see coming, so the opponent feels thoughtful."
- "As a player on Easy, I want the AI to under-bank compared to higher difficulties, so difficulty still matters."
- "As a developer, I want a distinct banking-aware strategy I can select in Monte Carlo and tune per difficulty, without risking regression in the existing Greedy baseline."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New banking-aware strategy (separate from Greedy):** A new `BankingGreedyStrategy` class is added alongside the existing `GreedyStrategy` — Greedy is left unchanged; `RandomStrategy` is unchanged. The new strategy implements `MainStreetAiStrategy` and is selectable by name (e.g. `BankingGreedy` / `banking-greedy`) wherever strategies are chosen.

2. **Deliberate hoarding behaviour:** The new strategy can choose `end-turn` even when `actionsRemaining > 0` when hoarding is higher-value than spending. When the heuristic's expected value of banking exceeds the best immediate spend's value, the AI banks; otherwise it spends normally via the existing Greedy scoring/priority logic.

3. **Hybrid banking heuristic with difficulty-scaled look-ahead (Q1c + Q3 + Q6):** A new scoring function evaluates the value of banking by considering (a) currently visible unaffordable high-value targets — in hand and in the market row — and (b) anticipated near-future targets via look-ahead into the market/deck pipeline. The heuristic factors current `bankedActions`, the target's cost vs. available coins, and the AI planning horizon (`aiPlanningHorizon()` from CG-0MSN1A71G005AF7W). Look-ahead depth / banking aggressiveness is reduced at lower difficulties (e.g., Easy banks rarely / looks only at visible cards, Hard considers deeper look-ahead and banks more aggressively). The exact tuning is documented in code comments and validated by tests.

4. **Bank-cap handling — natural via heuristic (Q4: producer leaves to implementer):** No special-case "always bank" branch; the heuristic naturally handles the cap — at `bankedActions == 2` the value of further banking is zero/negative, so the AI spends. Spending and cap enforcement already come from the engine (Q4 accepted as implementer's call to let the heuristic govern).

5. **Monte Carlo harness integration as a new strategy variant (Q5: new):** The Monte Carlo harness (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`) registers a new strategy name distinct from `greedy` (e.g., `banking-greedy`) so runs can compare baseline Greedy vs. banking-aware. Guardrail tests (`monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts` or equivalent) stay green within tolerance for the new strategy (or a drift report + baseline update is produced per policy CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2); existing `greedy`/`random` baselines are not silently replaced.

6. **Tests — deterministic banking scenarios:** Unit tests in `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` (new) cover, deterministically: (a) the new strategy hoards when a visible high-cost target exists that is currently unaffordable, (b) it spends when no valuable future target justifies hoarding, (c) it does not over-hoard (banks toward cap then spends), (d) it respects action-budget limits and existing legality constraints, (e) difficulty scaling — Easy hoards less than Hard given the same state. Existing `ai-action-budget` and `monte-carlo` tests remain green.

7. **Documentation:** `docs/main-street/` (or equivalent) and in-code comments document the new strategy's existence, when it banks vs. spends, and how difficulty scales look-ahead/aggressiveness. No tutorial changes (Q7: no).

## Constraints

- **Main Street only** — no core-engine changes.
- **Additive strategy:** `GreedyStrategy` and `RandomStrategy` are left unchanged; the banking-aware behaviour lives in a new class so existing behaviour can still be baseline-tested.
- **Bank cap 2, at-most-1 banked per day, day-start composition `1 + gmBonus + min(2, banked)` — all unchanged**; spending / capping comes from the engine. Engine correctly decrements banked on action spend (fix at CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC).
- **Hybrid heuristic required (Q1c):** consider both immediate visible targets and look-ahead, with look-ahead reduced at lower difficulties (Q1 parenthetical) and overall aggressiveness scaled by difficulty (Q6: yes).
- **Banking-aware strategy is a new Monte Carlo strategy name (Q5):** do not replace the existing `greedy` entry.
- **Tutorial unaffected (Q7: no)** — tutorial coverage for action banking remains the separate item CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P.
- **Prerequisite:** Bank-consumption fix CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC (in_review) — banking-aware AI builds on its corrected `consumeAction` semantics; track the dependency and adapt if that fix's semantics shift.

## Existing State

- `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `GreedyStrategy` with an 11-step priority chain (play business/upgrade from hand, buy upgrade, buy business, move-to-hand, buy event, play event, discard, community favour, hire staff, end-turn) and horizon-scored business/upgrade valuators. No banking concept. `RandomStrategy` is budget-oblivious uniform pick. Both respect budget only via `enumerateLegalActions` filtering.
- `MainStreetState.ts` — `bankedActions: number` field (init 0), serialized/deserialized, included in undo/redo snapshots.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts` / `MainStreetCommands.ts` — `executeDayStart` composes `bankedActions` into the day budget; `processEndOfTurn` banks unused actions; engine/command spend paths decrement `bankedActions` (fix at CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC, in_review).
- `MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — runs `GreedyStrategy` / `RandomStrategy` across seeds and difficulties (`MonteCarloStrategy = 'market-greedy' | 'demo-greedy' | 'greedy' | 'random'`); guardrail tests compare to `docs/main-street/monte-carlo-baseline.json`.
- `aiPlanningHorizon()` (CG-0MSN1A71G005AF7W) — `clamp(ceil((winThreshold - score)/8), 5, 25)` used for scoring business/upgrade income over future turns; available to reuse for banking valuation.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/ai-action-budget.test.ts` validates AI respects the action budget; does not test banking-aware decisions.

## Desired Change

Add a new `BankingGreedyStrategy` that wraps/extends the existing Greedy valuation but first evaluates an implicit "bank actions" option: score the best immediate legal spend vs. score the expected value of banking one action given visible + look-ahead targets and difficulty-scaled look-ahead depth. When banking wins, return `end-turn` early (deliberate hoard); otherwise delegate to the standard Greedy priority chain. Register the new strategy under a distinct name in the Monte Carlo harness so `banking-greedy` can be run and guarded separately from `greedy`.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Add `BankingGreedyStrategy` (and supporting `scoreBankOption()` / look-ahead helpers); leave `GreedyStrategy` and `RandomStrategy` unchanged; document difficulty scaling in comments.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Register new `banking-greedy` strategy name (extend `MonteCarloStrategy` union + `ALL_STRATEGIES`, wire `createAiPlayerForStrategy`); keep existing `greedy` path unchanged.
- `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` (new) — Deterministic unit tests for (a) hoard vs. spend, (b) no over-hoard to cap-then-spend, (c) budget legality, (d) difficulty-scaled aggressiveness, (e) hybrid visible + look-ahead triggers.
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts` (or new guardrail file) — Include/validate the new strategy; drift report + baseline update if intentionally shifted, per CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2 policy.
- `docs/main-street/` — AI behaviour section documenting the new strategy and difficulty scaling.

## Related Work

- **CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR** (completed) — Action banking mechanic (state + engine + UI + tests). Prerequisite this builds on.
- **CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC** (in_review) — Bank consumption fix (decrement banked on action via shared `consumeAction`). Prerequisite for correct banking semantics.
- **CG-0MSX41S7I009MMZN** (completed) — AI & Monte Carlo action budget awareness — existing tests validate AI respects budget.
- **CG-0MSN1A71G005AF7W** (completed) — AI threshold-distance planning horizon (`aiPlanningHorizon`) — reused for banking valuation.
- **CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R** (completed) — Base action economy (`actionsRemaining`, `actionsPerTurn`).
- **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** (open) — Tutorial coverage for action banking. Explicitly out of scope here per Q7.
- **CG-0MM4RG1GM0SRVENC** (completed) — PRD Milestone 6 extraction/refactoring (automated find_related match).
- **Automated find_related** at intake start also surfaced repo file matches under `example-games/main-street/` and `tests/main-street/` consistent with the Key Files above; full report sidecar at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-CG-0MT3JMGA60091J8W.md`.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Monte Carlo baseline drift:** Banking-aware runs may shift win-rate / coin-per-turn. Per CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2 policy produce a drift report and re-baseline only when the shift is intentional (not a hidden regression).
- **Look-ahead complexity:** Hybrid visible + deck look-ahead is more complex than visible-only; scope the look-ahead narrowly (few cards ahead / top of deck) and gate depth by difficulty to keep the strategy testable. If look-ahead proves too noisy, narrow to visible targets with a documented fallback.
- **Over-/under-hoarding:** Too aggressive ⇒ AI seems passive; too timid ⇒ no observable banking. Mitigate with difficulty-scaled thresholds and the four deterministic tests in AC6.
- **Dependency on CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC:** If the bank-consumption fix's semantics change before it lands, this strategy's valuation must adapt — track the dependency.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Per-difficulty Strategy parameter objects, hint-system integration, or re-tunable economy rebalancing are out of scope — record as linked work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1 — Banking heuristic trigger: "What determines when the AI should bank vs. spend? (a) visible unaffordable high-value targets, (b) look-ahead at market/deck, (c) hybrid?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01, this session): "c (where look ahead is reduced at lower difficulty levela)".** Source: interactive reply this session. Research: inspected `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` (Greedy priority chain + `aiPlanningHorizon`), `MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` strategy wiring, and `MainStreetState.ts` banked fields (see context-gathering in prior intake). Resolved: hybrid visible + look-ahead, with reduced look-ahead at lower difficulties.
- Q2 — Strategy granularity: "Parameter on GreedyStrategy, new BankingGreedyStrategy, or modify Greedy in place?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "new".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: additive new class; Greedy and Random left unchanged.
- Q3 — Hoarding depth: "How far ahead should the AI plan; leverage aiPlanningHorizon?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "yes".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: reuse `aiPlanningHorizon()` for banking valuation alongside the new heuristic.
- Q4 — Bank cap interaction: "When already at cap (2), still evaluate banking or handle via heuristic?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "your call".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: implementer's call — heuristic naturally returns zero/negative value at cap so the AI spends; no special-case branch (documented in AC4).
- Q5 — Monte Carlo strategy variant: "New banking-greedy name or replace existing greedy?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "new".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: distinct `banking-greedy` strategy name; existing `greedy`/`random` unchanged.
- Q6 — Difficulty tuning: "Should banking aggressiveness vary by difficulty?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "yes".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: aggressiveness / look-ahead depth scales with difficulty (Easy less aggressive than Hard).
- Q7 — Tutorial: "Does tutorial need to cover banking-aware AI?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "no".** Source: same session reply. Resolved: no tutorial changes; tutorial banking remains CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P.

# Intake Brief — Remove 'Market cycled...' activity log (CG-0MT5VXSSQ003O5ZC)

## Problem statement

Main Street's end-of-turn market cycling emits a noisy `Market cycled: N unpurchased cards moved to discard` entry on every turn. This adds little player value and clutters the activity log. The entry should be removed so the log only surfaces player-meaningful events.

## Users

- **Player** — reads the activity log to understand what happened each turn (purchases, income, events, gains/losses); does not want routine housekeeping noise.
- **Developer/QA** — validates log output against expectations; fewer spurious entries makes log assertions stable.

### User stories

- As a player, I want the activity log to omit routine `Market cycled...` notifications so I can focus on meaningful turn outcomes.

# Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street

## Problem Statement

Main Street is single-player only; the `MainStreetState`, `MainStreetEngine`, and PRD M3 were never designed for an opponent. Players asked for competitive play — racing an AI on the shared street grid — but the engine assumes single ownership of coins, hand, actions, street slots, and score. Adding competitive mode requires splitting those concerns while preserving single-player behaviour and the existing AI/hint/Monte Carlo stack.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player (competitive mode):** As a Main Street player, I want to play against an AI opponent on the same shared street so each turn I have a rival to race and react to.
- **Developer / QA:** As a developer, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.
- **Future AI iteration:** As an AI developer, I want the AI decision layer ownership-aware and staff-free so competitive strategy is coherent without rewriting the hint/balance harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Per-player state & ownership:** A competitive state model exists with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget, and score, plus owner-tagged street slots; deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG. Single-player behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC2 — AI plays a legal competitive turn:** The AI generates legal actions through `enumerateLegalActions` (competitive mode) with staff actions excluded, scored by an ownership-aware `scoreAction`/helpers, and executed via `executeAction`. Verified with legality and determinism tests.
- [ ] **AC3 — Per-owner income; shared events:** Income accrues only to the owning player of each placed business; street-wide investment events and incidents retain their existing resolution semantics, routed per-owner as specified. Validated by income/event unit tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Competitive Monte Carlo harness:** A head-to-head harness (extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) runs >=200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics; single-player AI tests still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Engine-only scope confirmed:** PRD M3 is updated to note this deliberate scope extension; competitive mode has no game-selector entry or scene yet — rendering (owner-coloured street, shared-market phase alternation with SFX/animations per AGENTS.md 8) is deferred to a planning-created child.
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests & docs:** Relevant unit tests and new tests cover AC1–AC4; build succeeds; affected docs/comments are updated.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full test suite passes** with the new changes (release gate; not a per-push requirement beyond `npm run build` + unit tests).

## Constraints

- Competitive mode scope is **state + engine + AI + Monte Carlo only** — no game selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome yet (AC5 deferred to a planning child).
- Turn alternation: **alternate MarketPhases within a shared day** (confirmed producer decision). Income/Incident/EndCheck phases are shared once both players have acted. Implementation design stays within planning.
- Win condition: **first player to reach the win threshold wins**; the game offers an endless continuation option beyond threshold (confirmed producer decision). Endless mode wiring is within the parent unless planning creates a dedicated child.
- `MainStreetAiPlayer` / `MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `enumerateLegalActions` are unchanged for single-player consumers.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved; replays remain reproducible.

## Existing State

- Single-player-only state (`MainStreetState` resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining), engine (`applyIncome`, `resolveEvent`, `resolveIncident`, `computeScore`, `checkEndConditions`), PRD M3, and AI layers (`MainStreetAiStrategy`, `GreedyStrategy`, `scoreAction`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`, `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) built for one owner. Reusability findings documented in the original description.
- One child item already exists: **CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (ownership-aware, staff-free)**.

## Desired Change

Ship an **engine-level competitive mode**: per-player state + owner-tagged grid, per-owner income routing, shared event semantics, ownership-aware and staff-free AI scoring, and a competitive Monte Carlo harness — without changing single-player behaviour or adding competitive rendering. Record the scope extension in PRD M3 and plan the rendering/scene child for the next milestone.

## Decisions Since Original Item

- **Turn structure:** Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) confirmed by producer.
- **AC5:** Deferred to planning — will become a child for rendering/selector/scene work.
- **Denial reasoning:** Opponent-aware denial (blocking best slot, buying to deny) intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- **Win condition:** First to threshold wins, with an endless continuation option beyond threshold.
- **Owner-coloured street (AC5):** Means tinting each placed business's street slot by owner (e.g., player = blue, AI = red) so the shared grid's ownership is visually unambiguous.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Split to per-player resources/hand/staff/actions/score; owner-tagged `StreetGrid` slots.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Per-owner income, shared event/incident routing, shared-day phase handling, competitive helpers.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness (extension).
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` — Note competitive mode as deliberate scope extension beyond M3.
- `tests/main-street/*.test.ts` (+ new competitive tests) — Unit + deterministic replay coverage for AC1–AC4; existing guardrails still passing.

## Related Work

- Related work items (from `find_related`): CG-0MM5ZGB8U02S0BFO — Main Street Scenario & Tutorial (completed) · CG-0MOXGGZXJ002X6H3 — [test-failure] MainStreetScene animation scheduling (completed) · CG-0MS9NXIEX00880UV — [test-failure] hud-layer-contract (completed)
- Related docs (from repo scan): `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` · `docs/DEVELOPER.md` · `AGENTS.md`
- Child: CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (existing; align description with this parent's clarified ACs).
- Existing state/engine/AI/monte-carlo layers are the implementation basis (see Existing State above).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **State split regressions in single player:** score/income/event paths silently ignore per-player split. Mitigation: keep single-player API shim and run full single-player regression suite.
- **Income/event routing divergence:** per-owner bugs hard to diagnose. Mitigation: explicit per-owner unit fixtures + deterministic replay across seeds.
- **AI ownership semantics under-tested:** greedy heuristics mis-score denial/synergy when ownership added. Mitigation: head-to-head harness + baseline comparisons (AC4).
- **Phase alternation complexity:** alternating MarketPhases within one day adds state machine edge cases. Mitigation: diagram shared-day phases in planning and cover transitions with unit tests.
- **Scope creep toward rendering:** temptation to start the selector/scene early. Mitigation: AC5 is explicitly deferred; new rendering asks become planning-linked children.

## Open Questions

None — all open intake questions have been answered by the producer (see Comments). Remaining design detail (per-player state shape, phase machine, Monte Carlo metrics schema, endless-mode trigger) is within planning.

- Q1 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Alternating turn structure — Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) vs Option B (alternate full days)?" — Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "a" → resolved as **Option A** (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day). Recorded in `wl comment` (producer decisions comment).
- Q2 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Child item coverage for AC5 — create competitive-scene child now or defer to planning?" — Answer (producer): "planning. for now what do you mean by 'owner colored streets'" → resolved as **deferred to planning**; follow-up clarification Q5 added. Recorded in `wl comment`.
- Q3 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Denial reasoning scope — deferred or minimum viable?" — Answer (producer): "deferred" → denial is **out of scope** for this epic, may become a follow-up child.
- Q4 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Win condition — first to threshold, fixed days, or simultaneous?" — Answer (producer): "when one player rea hes a win conditiion with option to carry on in endless mode" → **first to threshold wins, with endless continuation option**.
- Q5 (Map, implicit follow-up): "What does 'owner coloured streets' mean?" — Answer purpose: rendering the shared street grid where each placed business slot is visually tinted by owner (e.g., player blue, AI red) so ownership is immediately readable. Scene concern deferred to planning child.

# Intake Brief: Add a close business option to Main Street (CG-0MT5XT7K3005IBBV)

## Problem statement

In Main Street, a business/community-space card on the street grid can only be **sold**, which refunds 50% of purchase+upgrade cost and leaves the card **permanently on the grid** in an inert "sold" state — the slot stays occupied for the rest of the game (placement requires an empty slot). Players need a **Close** option: an action-consuming, coin-free action that **removes the card from the street entirely**, freeing the slot so a new card can be placed there later.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants to replace an underperforming business instead of being stuck with a dead sold card in a key slot.

**Example user stories:**

- "As a player, I want to close a business that is losing money (negative ongoing cost) so I can place a better card in that slot on a later day."
- "As a player, I want to clear a community-space card from the street without keeping it as a permanently occupied slot."
- "As a player, I want a clear, confirmable way to close a street card (costing 1 action, no coins) distinct from selling it (free, refund, stays on the grid)."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Scope & UI (feature behavior):** During `MarketPhase`, every **non-sold** business and community-space card on the street grid offers a **Close** option; **sold** cards never do. The existing click-a-street-card confirmation dialog (`showSellConfirmation`) is extended into a **Manage card** dialog with **[Sell] [Close] [Cancel]** buttons (reusing `createOverlayBackground`/`createOverlayButton`, HUD-container parenting, depth 199/200/201).
2. **Cost:** Closing consumes **exactly one daily action** via the shared `consumeAction` helper (`actionsRemaining` and `bankedActions` decremented, floor 0 — CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC) and grants **no coins**. Selling remains free and unchanged.
3. **Removal:** Closing removes the card from `streetGrid[slotIndex]` (slot → `null`), pushes it to the `discardPile` (not removed from the game), incrementally updates affected neighbors' cached income/synergy values, writes an activity-log entry, and the slot becomes **immediately placeable** by new cards.
4. **Undo & feedback:** Close is a **reversible command** (`closeBusinessCommand` via the undo manager restores the card, slot occupancy, action budget, and neighbor values) and is rendered with an **animation + SFX** consistent with the existing sell demolition (`animateSell`) and the event-driven audio rule (`COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, reduced-motion respected).
5. **Quality & docs:** Unit tests cover legality (MarketPhase, non-sold, slot occupied, action sufficiency), cost, removal, neighbor recalculation, and undo; a browser test covers the Manage-card dialog (Sell / Close / Cancel); HUD/help tooltips and docs are updated (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md` action-economy table: Close added under *action-consuming* operations, explicitly NOT in the "Free operations" list; GDD action-economy section; `ux-visual-audio.md` if the close animation differs); the **full test suite passes** (`npm test`) and the production build succeeds (`npm run build`).

## Constraints

- Action cost must go through the **single shared `consumeAction`** enforcement point (CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC) — same path as `buyBusinessCommand`/`buyAndPlaceBusinessCommand`; no double-decrement, no divergence.
- Follow the engine's existing patterns: `LegalityResult` discriminated union (`canCloseBusiness`), reversible `toCommand`/`snapshotAction` command, and `MainStreetMarket` action module structure mirroring `sellBusiness`/`canSellBusiness`.
- Modal dialog must follow the project's UI best practices (backdrop 199, box 200, interactive 201; parent all text/buttons into `hudContainer`; `dismissOverlay` cleanup) and SLL for positioning.
- Event-driven audio rule (CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N-context rule in AGENTS.md): the close action must be animated and sounded via the shared helpers/SoundManager; `shakeIllegalMove`/illegal feedback for rejected closes; reduced-motion and mute/volume settings respected.
- i18n: dialog/label strings should follow the game's i18n pattern if the existing sell dialog strings are localized.
- Doc-update policy: this is a rules/mechanic change — `docs/main-street/*` must be updated in the same change; create a doc-update child work item if it can't land in the same commit.

## Existing state

- **Sell from street:** `sellBusiness` (`MainStreetMarket.ts`) marks `soldSlots[slotIndex] = true`, refunds `Math.ceil((purchasePrice + upgradeCosts) / 2)`, card stays on grid (inert — no income/synergy), **free** (no action consumed). Legality gate `canSellBusiness` (MarketPhase only, unsold only). `updateNeighborsOnSale` recalcs neighbors.
- **UI entry:** clicking a non-sold street card in `MarketPhase` → `MainStreetTurnController.onSellCard` → `MainStreetOverlayContent.showSellConfirmation` (Sell/Cancel, refund text) → `sellBusinessCommand` (free).
- **Placement:** `canPlaceFromHand` requires `streetGrid[slotIndex] === null` — so a sold card permanently occupies its slot today.
- **Engine legacy helper:** `sellFromTableau` already models "remove card entirely + to discard pile", but is unused by the street UI and prices at 75% (old PRD semantics) — NOT to be reused for Close (Close pays nothing).
- **AI:** `enumerateLegalActions` does not enumerate street sells (player-initiated); no AI changes expected, but verify — costs/empty-slot should not break AI budget tests (`ai-action-budget.test.ts`).
- **Docs:** `core-rules-and-mechanics.md` lists "Selling a business" under **Free operations**; Close must be added as an action-consuming op.

## Desired change

Add a **Close** action alongside Sell for street-grid cards: click a non-sold card → Manage card dialog ([Sell] [Close] [Cancel]); Close costs **1 action, no coins**, removes the card from the grid (slot → null), sends it to the discard pile, recalcs neighbors, logs the activity, animates + sounds the removal, and is undoable. Sold cards remain permanently on the grid (unchanged) and are not closeable.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` — add `closeBusiness()` + `canCloseBusiness()` (+ `CloseResult`) mirroring the sell helpers; neighbor recalculation (reuse `updateNeighborsOnSale`-style logic)
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — add `closeBusinessCommand()` (consumes action via shared `consumeAction`; undo snapshot restores card/action/neighbors)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — extend `showSellConfirmation` into the Manage-card dialog (Sell / Close / Cancel) or add a parallel dialog
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — manage-card entry + close handler (legality, action-cost messaging, tutorial gating parity)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — street-card click/tooltip wiring (sold cards stay non-interactive; tooltip text)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — close removal animation + SFX (reuse/parallel `animateSell`)
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — tooltip copy if the free-ops list changes (Close must not appear there)
- `example-games/main-street/i18n/` — localized strings for the new dialog if sell strings are localized
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — verify enumeration/budget unaffected (should be, like street sell)
- Tests: `tests/main-street/CloseBusiness.test.ts` (unit: legality, cost, removal, neighbors, undo) + a browser dialog test (or extend `MainStreetSellCards.test.ts` / `MainStreetPlaceSell.test.ts`)
- Docs: `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (action-economy table), `docs/main-street/the-build-gdd.md` (action economy), `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` (close animation), game help text/README if they describe street-card actions

## Related work

- CG-0MTCP7F9S009HARC — shared `consumeAction` enforcement point (must be reused for Close's action cost)
- CG-0MT24X0SX007RLHN — same-day composite buy-and-place pricing (context for the action economy; Close must not affect it)
- CG-0MSLXJCHH001DLIO — no turn-limit default (close-as-action fits the longer-horizon economy)
- CG-0MQVJ4DIC009K8D8 — Scenario Validation Test (critical; close legality must not break scenario validation)

**Related work (automated report — /skill:find-related):**

- **CG-0MM4RFN5N0KTUR66** — Main Street: PRD Milestone 5 -- Tutorial, Onboarding, and Game Selector Integration (completed; tutorial-gating context for the new dialog)
- **CG-0MSKU0BE5003I2ZD** — Main Street: merge business hand + held event into one horizontal 3-card hand (completed; hand/street interaction context)
- **CG-0MQK7IQE9003LH7X** — panel status lines not working (completed; overlay/panel polish context)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** a closed card goes to the `discardPile` (consistent with `sellFromTableau`); it is not removed from the game, and it never returns to the market.
- **Risk — action economy:** Close is a new way to spend actions (effectively "demolish + refund-free sell" at the cost of 1 action). Monitor for degenerate play patterns (e.g., closing a card then immediately re-buying a better one each day); balance guardrails (`balance-guardrail-recommendations.md`) may need a follow-up review.
- **Risk — scope creep:** AI usage of Close, challenge interactions, tutorial/two-turn-step teaching updates, and stats/transcript schema changes are out of scope for this item — file follow-up work items if discovered during implementation.
- **Risk — sold-slot semantics:** sold cards permanently occupying slots is unchanged by this feature; a future "clear sold card" capability could be a separate work item.
- **Compatibility:** i18n coverage of new strings and browser-test interaction with tutorial gating must be checked; undo of Close must also restore the tutorial step state if gated.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Source: producer reply to intake questions comment, 2026-08-30.

- **Q3 (scope):** "Does Close apply to both business and community-space cards, and should sold (inert) cards be closeable?" — Answer (producer): **apply to all except sold** — both families are closeable; sold cards are not. Source: producer reply, 2026-08-30.
- **Q4 (discard) — noted assumption, not asked:** closed card → `discardPile` (slot → null, placeable). Open to revision if the producer prefers removal from the game.

# Intake Brief: Enable Main Street Expansion of Playing Area

## Problem Statement

Main Street currently has a single fixed 2×5 street (10 slots) with no ability to expand the playing field. The player should be able to zoom out at any time to reveal a larger 2D grid of streets, where each cell is a 2×5 street. Corner slots between streets are shared — one card serves all four adjacent streets, with normal adjacency rules.

## Users & User Stories

- **As a player**, I want to zoom out and explore neighbouring streets so that I can place more businesses and grow my empire beyond the initial 10-slot grid.
- **As a player**, I want shared corner plots between streets so that strategically placed businesses create cross-street synergy bonuses.
- **As a player**, I want the zoom to work like a map — smooth camera movement that reveals streets organically without gating or milestones.
- **As a game engine developer**, I want the grid system to be unbounded (or at least large enough to support extended play) so the game doesn't end prematurely when all streets are full.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Camera system**: A zoom/pan camera system is implemented for Main Street, allowing the player to zoom out to reveal neighbouring streets. The zoom is controlled by the player (e.g. scroll wheel or button), not gated by milestones.
2. **Grid topology**: The street grid is represented as a 2D lattice where each cell is a 2×5 street. Corner slots (where streets meet at the corners of adjacent 2×5 grids) are shared — one card slot serves the shared position, and the card is adjacent to neighbours in all four streets per normal adjacency rules.
3. **Adjacency & synergy**: The adjacency resolver (`MainStreetAdjacency.ts`) is updated to compute correct 8-way Chebyshev adjacency across street cells, including shared corner slots. Synergy bonuses and income calculations work correctly for cards on expanded streets and shared corners.
4. **Rendering**: All street cells within the current camera viewport are rendered. Cards placed on expanded or shared slots display and interact correctly. Unrevealed streets outside the current zoom level are not rendered.
5. **Save/Load**: The expanded grid state (all placed cards, including shared corner cards, and current zoom/camera position) serializes and deserializes correctly.

## Constraints

- The zoom is **always available** — no gating by milestones, turns, or resources.

# Main Street 64×64 Left-Art Card Redesign

## Goal

Redesign all Main Street card SVG generators to use a **64×64 left-art** layout where every card has a square graphic zone in the top-left area with text elements arranged to the right and below — no title overlap, hand-overlap aware, and future-proof for street stacking.

## Current State

All card types (`MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts`) use a **horizontal stack** layout:
- Header bar (20px) with centered title
- Text lines below: income/rep, trigger, cost circle (bottom-right), synergy icons (bottom-left)

This creates:
- **No visual identity** — cards are colour+text only
- **No graphic distinction** — all 4 families look similar
- **Poor hand overlap** — text is small and hard to read when cards overlap
- **No stacking identity** — stacked cards show no distinguishing art

## Target Layout

```
140×80 card (CARD_W=140, CARD_H=80)

┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│  ┌──────────────┐  Income: +230  │ header area (20px)
│  │              │  +5 ●/turn     │ graphic zone (64×64)
│  │   BREAD      │  ○○     (300)  │ at x=8, y=8
│  │              │                │ 64×64 square art
│  │  [64×64]     │                │ with 4px radius
│  │  graphic     │                │ title moves right
│  └──────────────┘                │ no overlap
│                                  │
│                                  │
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Key Principles

1. **Title moves right** — centered above graphic, moved to right-aligned or right-side text block
2. **64×64 graphic** — always in top-left (x=8, y=8), never overlaps title or text
3. **Hand overlap aware** — 64×64 art positioned so key visual survives HandView overlap
4. **Stacking ready** — graphic visible enough to distinguish when cards stack vertically

## Hand Overlap Analysis

HandView overlap: cards fan with ~20px gap. When overlapping:

```
Card N-1    Card N      Card N+1
┌────┐      ┌────┐      ┌────┐
│    │████████│    │████████│    │
│    │████████│    │████████│    │
└────┘      └────┘      └────┘
  20px        20px        20px
  overlap     overlap     overlap
```

With 64×64 at x=8:
- **Top edge visible**: 64 - 20 = **44px** survives overlap
- **Left edge visible**: 8px gutter survives (but only 8px)
- **Safe zone**: y=8..52 of the graphic is always visible
- **Critical content**: keep logo/key visual in top-center (y=8..52)

### Recommendation for Art Placement

Place the **logo/key visual in the top 48px** of the 64×64 zone. Bottom 16px can contain subtle pattern/texture that won't be visible during hand overlap but adds richness when card is fully revealed.

## Street Stacking Analysis

Future stacking: multiple staff cards (or other low-value cards) stacked underneath played cards.

```
Top card (visible)
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│  ┌──────────────┐  Income: +230  │
│  │   BREAD      │  +5 ●/turn     │
│  │              │  ○○     (300)  │
│  └──────────────┘                │
└──────────────────────────────────┘
Staff card underneath (partial)
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│  ┌──────────────┐  ● 1/turn      │  visible: top 15px
│  │   JANITOR    │                │  → graphic top 15px visible
│  └──────────────┘                │  → staff icon recognizable
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

With 64×64 at y=8:
- **Visible top**: 8 + 15 = **23px** of card (graphic top 15px)
- **Recognition threshold**: logo must be readable at ~23px height
- **Solution**: use **bold, high-contrast icons** (not subtle details)

### Stacking-Friendly Design Rules

1. **Icon-centric** — use large, simple icons (not detailed scenes)
2. **High contrast** — bright primary color against dark background
3. **Top-heavy** — key visual in top 40% of graphic (y=8..28)
4. **Color-coded** — synergy type color at top of graphic (reinforces identity)

## Card Family Specs

### Business/Community Space Cards
```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│  ┌──────────────┐  Income: +230  │ ← 10px green
```

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **All 5 card families** (business, community-space, event, upgrade, staff) use 64×64 left-art layout
2. **Title never overlaps** graphic zone — always positioned to the right (x≥76) or below graphic
3. **Hand overlap survives**: 64×64 graphic positioned so ≥44px vertical remains visible during HandView overlap
4. **Stacking readable**: graphic key visual identifiable at ~23px visible height (top-heavy design)
5. **No regression**: existing text elements (income, rep, cost, synergy icons, level badge) still present and legible
6. **All existing tests pass**: card generation, texture loading, market display, hand display
7. **SVG validates**: generated SVGs parse correctly, no overlapping elements, aria-label preserved
8. **Documentation updated**: card layout documented in `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` JSDoc

## Risks

- **Asset generation**: 155 cards × 5 families = need ~775 unique graphics (or reuse templates per family)
- **Backward compatibility**: saved games reference card textures — new layout = new texture keys
- **HandView overlap**: `HandView` may need adjustment if cards are wider at top (unlikely with same 140px total)
- **SVG performance**: `<image>` elements may be slower than `<rect>` fills — test with 20+ cards in view

- Actual artwork creation (use placeholder colored rects/icons for now)
